title: Building an Equation from Slope and Y-Intercept

scenes.title: You know the slope and the y-intercept. What is the equation?
scenes.narration: Suppose a line has slope negative three and y-intercept eight. What equation represents it? This is exactly what slope-intercept form is designed for.

scenes.title: What the symbols mean
body: m = slope = change in y for each 1 in x
scenes.narration: In y equals m x plus b, m is the slope, the rate of change. And b is the y-intercept, the value of y when x is zero.

scenes.title: Substitute the given values
scenes.narration: Now substitute the values directly. Replace m with negative three and b with eight. That gives y equals negative three x plus eight.

scenes.title: Check the meaning
body: Increase x by 1 -> y drops by 3
scenes.narration: Check it. At x equals zero, y equals eight, so the y-intercept is correct. Increase x by one and y drops from eight to five, then to two. That confirms a slope of negative three.

scenes.title: Recap
body: Put the slope in for m
Put the y-intercept in for b
scenes.narration: Recap: when the slope and y-intercept are already known, start with y equals m x plus b, substitute the slope for m, substitute the y-intercept for b, and simplify the signs. Here the equation is y equals negative three x plus eight. The full lesson is available on SUMMIT. Find the complete lesson below.
